title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 74
paragraphs: This Astyages, then, who was Cyrus’s mother’s father, Cyrus had conquered and made a prisoner, for a reason I shall declare in the history that follows. This, then, was the complaint Croesus had against Cyrus when he sent to the Oracles to ask whether he should march against the Persians; and when a deceitful answer had come back to him, he marched into the dominion of the Persians, supposing that the answer was favorable to himself. When Croesus came to the river Halys, then, according to my account, he passed his army across by the bridges that were there. But according to the account prevailing among the Greeks, Thales of Miletus enabled him to pass his army across. For they say that when Croesus was at a loss how his army should cross over the river—since, they add, at that time the bridges that now exist did not yet exist—Thales, who was present in the army, caused the river, which was then flowing on the left side of the army, to flow partly on the right as well. He did it in this way: beginning above the camp, he proceeded to dig a deep channel, directing it in the form of a crescent moon, so that the river, turned aside from its ancient course along this channel, would take the camp, which was pitched there, in the rear, and then, passing by the camp, would fall back into its ancient course. So as soon as the river was divided in two, it became fordable in both its branches. And some even say that the ancient course of the river was altogether dried up. But this tale I do not admit as true, for how then would they have crossed the river on their way back?
